School Values
Welcome
A very warm welcome to our school.It is my great privilege to welcome you to Niton Primary School, where every child is at the heart of all we do. We are proud to be a caring, inclusive and ambitious community where children are inspired to learn, encouraged to grow and supported to become the very best version of themselves.Our vision is built upon the values of Truth, Love, Respect, Friendship and Courage. These values are woven into every aspect of school life, shaping the way we learn together, care for one another and celebrate each other's achievements. They provide the strong foundation upon which our children develop not only as successful learners but also as kind, thoughtful and responsible members of society.We believe that every child is unique, bringing their own talents, interests and aspirations to our school family. From the moment they walk through our doors, they are welcomed into a nurturing environment where they are known, valued and respected as individuals. We strive to ensure that every child feels safe, happy and confident, enabling them to flourishacademically, socially, emotionally and personally.As a school, we are committed to creating an environment where every child can thrive. We have high expectations for all our pupils and believe that every child has the potential to achieve great things. Through an exciting, broad and enriching curriculum, combined with exceptional care and support, we both challenge and nurture our children so they can discovertheir strengths, develop resilience and reach their true potential.Our school is much more than a place of learning—it is a community and a family. We cherish the strong relationships that exist between children, staff, parents and the wider community, recognising that by working together we create the very best opportunities for our pupils. We celebrate diversity, encourage curiosity and foster a genuine sense of belonging, ensuring that every child feels proud to be part of our school.We want our children to leave us with a lifelong love of learning, confidence in their own abilities and the courage to embrace new challenges. Above all, we hope they leave with happy memories, lasting friendships and the values that will guide them throughout their lives.Whether you are considering joining our school, are already part of our community or are simply visiting our website, I hope you gain a real sense of the warmth, ambition and care that make our school such a special place. We would be delighted to welcome you to visit us and experience first-hand the happy, purposeful atmosphere that enables every child to shine.I look forward to welcoming you and your family into our school community.With warmest wishes,Mrs Kirsty ThomasActing Headteacher

Special Educational Needs (SEND)
SENDCo Lead – Mrs Charlotte Reddecliff
Inclusion & Special Educational Needs
Together with the teachers and extra adults in school, we are here to help make a positive difference for those children who most need it. We aim to work in partnership with parents, families, outside agencies such as Speech and Language Therapists, Educational Psychologists, Doctors, feeder pre-schools, IOW Family Centres and secondary schools.
We offer a range of interventions and ways of supporting learning; it is important that we identify your child’s needs and provide support for them to learn, feel good about themselves and find ways of achieving success.
Please click HERE to go to the Policy section to view our SEND Policy and Accessibility Plan.
Please click HERE to view our SEND Information Report 2024-2025.
How We Work
If you have any concerns about your child’s needs in communication and interaction, learning, social, emotional or mental health and/or physical/sensory areas then ask to have a chat with the class teacher. Mrs Reddecliff is on site every day and you are welcome to call into the office or phone to arrange a time to meet with us.
We follow the national Code of Practice for Special Educational Needs and Disability (2015)
SEN Support
Where a child has been identified as needing SEN Support we will make sure we take positive steps to remove barriers to learning. We will follow a Graduated Approach of ‘assess, plan, do, review’ to ensure the child makes good progress and achieves good outcomes through High Quality Inclusive Teaching and where required, evidence based interventions.
Statement/Education Health Care Plan
For a small percentage of children they will have a statement of SEN or an Education Health Care Plan (EHCP) issued by the Local Authority. Their needs must first be assessed through a statutory assessment.Schools and parents can request this if the child’s needs meet the criteria set by the Local Authority.
At each stage there will be shared conversations with parents/carers. We will work together.
All children with a Special Educational Need will have a Pupil Centred Profile (PCP). This will be shared with you at each Parent Consultation meeting. It will look like this:

The Isle of Wight Council is committed to giving all children and young people high quality education that enables them to make progress and achieve well. For children and young people aged 0-25 with special educational needs or a disability, additional or specialist support may be needed to enable this. To support the process of identifying the range of provision and advice that is available, the Isle of Wight Local Authority have published a local offer (click here to view).

Before and After School Club
Sunrise Breakfast Club
We are open from 7.45am to 8.30am Monday to Friday
Sunrise Club
Our aim at Niton Primary Sunrise Club is to provide a happy, safe, warm andstimulating environment for all our children to have fun, play and learn. We have threemembers of qualified, experienced staff working before and after school throughout the week.
Please download the School Gateway App (instructions on how to HERE) to book your child on to Sunrise sessions. Bookings can be made online up to 10pm the night before.
Sunset After School Club
Niton Preschool run the Sunset after school provision. They offer an Afterschool Club running from 3:10pm to 5:30pm
During school holidays, their Summer Holiday Club operates from 7:30am to 5:30pm, offering a safe, engaging space for your child.
Please download the School Gateway App (instructions on how to HERE) to book your child on to Sunset sessions.

Extra - Curricular Clubs
At Niton, we believe that learning doesn’t stop when the bell rings! Our extra-curricular clubs provide pupils with exciting opportunities to explore new interests, develop talents, and build friendships outside the classroom.
We provide a range of free clubs for pupils. The clubs on offer are updated each half term; parents and carers are sent a letter that includes a link to sign up.
Clubs on offer Autumn Term (September - December)
All clubs will begin from the week commencing Monday 7th September 2026 until Friday 12th December 2026

Please remember that we would love to welcome in parents to run clubs – do you have a skill you would be happy to share? Please note that all volunteers will need to have a DBS check before running a club.
